title: PRD: Weighted-signal framework and A/B thresholds for Optimize evals
creator: Alicia Chen
description: Purpose: Define a product requirements document for a weighted-signal evaluation framework and concrete A/B/canary thresholds for Optimize. The goal is to (1) standardize how we combine multiple signals (quality, safety, latency, cost) into a gating decision, (2) codify statistical rules and minimum sample sizes for A/B tests and canaries, and (3) define automatic rollback/stop criteria that integrate with the Redwood rollout API. This ticket captures scope, acceptance criteria, monitoring and runbook requirements, and handoffs to engineering and analytics.
acceptance_criteria: A canonical signal weighting matrix exists (weights for: human-rated quality, safety incidents, hallucination rate, latency P95, token cost) and is stored as a JSON spec in the Optimize config repo.
For the default product lane, weighted-score regression of >1.5% (absolute) vs baseline on the combined score fails the gating check and prevents rollout progression.
Safety regressions are evaluated independently: any increase in high-severity safety hits >0.05% absolute triggers an immediate canary stop regardless of combined score.

A/B tests require minimum N=1,000 impressions per variant for primary PRD prompt sets; for low-volume prompt sets the system enforces 'extended test' mode with adjusted thresholds and a minimum of N=3,000.

Statistical significance requirement: two-sided chi-squared or bootstrap for non-binary metrics with p-value < 0.05 and pre-registered metric directionality. Confidence intervals must be reported in dashboards.
Latency regression: P95 increase >10% AND >50ms absolute causes fail for latency-sensitive routes; routes flagged as latency-sensitive are configurable per model route.
A/B uplift pass criteria: a positive delta in weighted-score must be >=0.5 percentage points and statistically significant to be considered 'win' for rollout automation.
Runbook entries exist for automated rollback: which alerts fire, who is paged, and which manual checks can override automatic rollback (with audit log).
Implementation includes an 'evaluation spec' UI in Console to visualize metric weights, alert thresholds, and per-prompt-set sample counts.
decisions: Adopt a weighted-score aggregator instead of single-metric gates to reduce false positives from noisy signals.
Expose both combined-score and per-signal breakouts in dashboards — automation uses combined score but rollbacks are aware of the per-signal rationale.
Default A/B significance level will be 0.05; product teams can opt into stricter thresholds via the evaluation spec.
Canary default traffic split: 2% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with minimum dwell time of 60 minutes at each step unless faster promotion is explicitly allowed.
Immediate-stop safety rules are hard-coded and cannot be relaxed via rollout config without an explicit approval from Security & Trust.
monitoring_plan: Create an Optimize 'Eval Gate' dashboard showing: weighted score trend, individual signal time series (quality, safety, hallucination, latency, cost), sample counts, and p-values.
Add pre-configured alerts: weighted_score_drop, safety_high_sev_increase, latency_p95_increase, sample_rate_degradation. Alerts surface in Slack channel #optimize-evals and pager rotation.
Dashboards show rolling windows (30m, 3h, 24h) and compare canary to baseline with CIs.
Store evaluation artifacts (seeded promptset, randomization seed, and metric outputs) in a retention bucket for 90 days for audit and debugging.
rollout_plan: Canary flow: automated evaluation at each step. If gating checks pass, rollout advances automatically; on fail, automated rollback and incident creation.
Manual override: product owners can pause or abort canary with an approval workflow that is logged in the audit trail.
Staged rollouts for enterprise customers: ability to pin to dedicated capacity and apply separate thresholds (enterprise lanes configured in spec).
Integration with existing rollout API GH action (link below) to ensure rollout decisions can be enacted programmatically.
testing_signals: Human-rated quality: aggregated from the Optimize promptset tagging UI; conversion into a normalized 0-100 score.
Safety: binary and severity-graded labels; create per-category thresholds (toxicity, PII leakage, disallowed content).
Hallucination proxy: factuality check pass-rate vs ground-truth where available.
Latency: P50/P95/P99 per-route and per-model. Use HLS (histogram-based) comparisons to detect distributional shifts.
Cost: per-token effective cost delta after batching and quantization applied; include short-term and steady-state estimates.
review_feedback: @ProductLead: request clearer guidance on how to weight customer-visible regressions vs infra metrics (latency/cost). Suggest +10% relative weight to customer-facing quality signals for public routes.
@Security: accept immediate-stop safety rule but require an emergency response runbook link; security review to sign off before release.
@Analytics: flagged need for instrumentation around sample tagging and deterministic randomization seeds for reproducible A/B tests.
